header: The full calculator, laid out like the Mac's: BASIC (four columns) and SCIENTIFIC (ten columns: brackets, memory, powers, roots, logs, trig, hyperbolic, 2nd, Rad/Deg, EE), no converters in it. I made the function keys grey, the number keys darker and the operators orange (the pending one lights up white). It works with the mouse, the touch and the keyboard (digits, + - * /, Enter, Backspace, Delete). In the scientific calculator a second switch, DEC · BIN · OCT · HEX, writes the number in that base (whole numbers; the keys the base does not have are greyed, and in HEX the six trig keys of the left block become A-F, so the panel keeps its size). In another base the line under the number shows it in the other bases. All the arithmetic is in src/tools/calculator/calcEngine.ts (a pure state machine, tested). Nothing is stored or sent: the memory and the history are only in this window.

symbols.name: KEY_RATIO
doc: I size everything in the calculator from one height, --calc-h (the same for the basic and the scientific calculator, so that they are equally tall). From it come the key height --calc-d (a twelfth-part of it, as in the Mac's), the padding, the gaps, the display, the width of each calculator, the radius, and every size of text below, as a share of --calc-d. The basic keys are circles (width = height = d); the scientific keys are 1.24 d wide, the Mac's 62 : 50.

doc: `startBase` and `startValue` open the scientific calculator on a value in a base (a typed "0xFF"); pass `autoFocus` false when it is drawn while the user is still typing in the search line.

behaviours: the scientific calculator has the base switch with DEC, BIN, OCT, HEX, in that order; the basic one does not
the switch shows the base in use: DEC selected at first, HEX selected when opened on a hex number
THE PANEL KEEPS ITS SIZE AND KEYS: the same width and height, the same grid of 10 columns and 5 rows, and the same number of keys, in DEC, BIN and HEX (only the six keys' faces change)
in HEX the six trig keys (Sine, Cosine, Tangent, Hyperbolic sine, cosine, tangent) are the digits A to F, in the same places in the grid
in DEC the digits A to F do not exist; in BIN the trig keys stay (greyed)
BIN: the digits 2 to 9 are greyed (disabled) and 0 and 1 are not; the point, sin, √ and π are greyed; the four rules and = are live
HEX: A to F and 0 to 9 are live; the point and π are greyed
DEC: no key is greyed, as before
a number in HEX is shown in HEX (FF), with a HEX badge, and the other bases under it: DEC 255 · BIN 1111 1111 · OCT 377
in BIN the number is grouped in fours (1111 1111) and the line under it gives DEC, OCT and HEX; the copy button copies it without the spaces
in DEC the line under the number is still the Indian words (255: two hundred fifty-five), not the bases, and there is no base badge
the card opened on a typed number does not take the keyboard from the search line (autoFocus false), and does when opened as a form (the default)

a long number gets smaller to fit its one line: 66 characters of DEC go to 0.34 of a key (the floor), of BIN to 0.35 (its narrow digits take more characters: 24 where decimal holds 15, measured in a browser), and never below 0.22; a short one keeps 0.95
a 53-digit binary number is on the display whole (grouped, 66 characters), with its other bases under it
